steps.title: Steady state, hypothesis
steps.caption: Steady state from outside: 99.9% success. Hypothesis: losing 1 of 3 instances keeps it above 99.5%.
steps.body: First describe *working* from the outside: checkout success is **99.9%** at about **1,200 orders a minute**, measured at the load balancer. Then write a **hypothesis** that predicts it stays that way: if one of the three Checkout instances is terminated, success stays above 99.5%. The card also records the fault, the **blast radius** (one instance) and the **stop condition** (success below 99%), and the run is set for working hours with the on-call team told.

steps.title: Inject a small failure
steps.caption: One instance is terminated in production: the load balancer routes around it and success holds.
steps.body: During normal traffic one instance is terminated. A request in flight fails, the load balancer's health check takes the instance out, the other two take 600 orders a minute each, and auto scaling starts a replacement. Success dips to 99.8% and recovers: the **hypothesis holds**, and the confidence that losing an instance is harmless now rests on evidence.

steps.title: Find a weakness, stop
steps.caption: Payments slowed by 2 s: with no timeout, calls pile up; below 99% the guardrail stops the run.
steps.body: The next experiment adds **2 s of latency** to 5% of Payments calls. Checkout has no timeout on that call, so its workers wait, requests pile up and success falls; when it drops below 99% the **stop condition** fires, the fault is removed automatically and the metric recovers. The finding: the Payments call needs a [timeout and a fallback](../timeout-and-fallback/).

steps.title: Fix, rerun, make routine
steps.caption: With a timeout and fallback the rerun passes. It then runs weekly, and the blast radius grows.
steps.body: With a 1 s timeout and a fallback (the order is accepted as *payment pending* and charged moments later), the same experiment passes. It is then **automated** to run every week, the blast radius grows in steps (next: a whole zone instead of one instance), and **game days** rehearse the people and runbooks as well as the software.
